skill.name: golang-performance
skill.description: Golang performance optimization guidance for profiled bottlenecks, covering allocation reduction, CPU efficiency, memory layout, GC tuning, pooling, caching, I/O, and hot-path review.
skill.summary: Apply profiling-driven Go performance patterns and validate each change with benchmarks.
skill.author: samber

security_audit.summary: All static findings were adjudicated as false positives. The matches occur in Markdown documentation, JSON evaluation prompts, example Go snippets, local profiling commands, or project metadata, with no evidence of malicious execution, exfiltration, prompt injection, or unauthorized file access.

content.value_statement: Go services often slow down from allocations, GC pressure, I/O waits, or inefficient hot paths. This skill maps profiling signals to focused Go performance fixes and benchmark validation.
actual_capabilities: Maps pprof, fgprof, trace, and benchmark signals to specific Go optimization patterns.
Guides allocation reduction, slice reuse, map sizing, pooling, and backing array fixes.
Explains CPU hot-path improvements, cache locality, inlining, false sharing, and SIMD tradeoffs.
Covers runtime tuning for GC, GOMEMLIMIT, GOMAXPROCS, and profile-guided optimization.
Provides review guidance for I/O, networking, caching, batching, and observability regressions.
limitations: Requires profiling data or a clearly identified bottleneck for best results.
Does not replace production load testing or statistically sound benchmarks.
Go tool availability depends on the local project environment.
External service, database, or infrastructure bottlenecks may need other skills.

use_cases.title: Review a Slow API Handler
use_cases.description: Identify whether latency comes from Go code, database calls, network waits, allocations, or JSON overhead.

use_cases.title: Reduce Allocation Pressure
use_cases.description: Use heap profiles and benchmarks to choose slice, map, pooling, or copy strategies.

use_cases.title: Prevent Performance Regressions
use_cases.description: Add benchmark comparisons, Prometheus checks, and documentation for optimized hot paths.

prompt_templates.title: Start With Profiling
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a slow Go service.
prompt_templates.prompt: My Go service is slow, but I do not know the bottleneck. Help me choose profiling steps before changing code.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Heap Pressure
prompt_templates.prompt: I have a heap profile showing high allocations in a Go function. Explain likely causes and propose one benchmarked change at a time.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize a Hot Path
prompt_templates.prompt: This Go function dominates CPU time in pprof. Review it for inlining, cache locality, allocation, and algorithmic improvements.

prompt_templates.title: Design Regression Checks
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create benchmark, benchstat, and observability checks that catch Go performance regressions before release.

output_examples.input: A handler has high latency but low CPU use.
output_examples.output: The response should first check off-CPU waits, blocked goroutines, tracing spans, and upstream calls before micro-optimizing code.

output_examples.input: A heap profile shows many short-lived buffer allocations.
output_examples.output: The response should compare slice reuse, bounded pooling, and safe copy rules, then ask for benchmark validation.

output_examples.input: A benchmark shows a loop dominates CPU time.
output_examples.output: The response should inspect algorithmic complexity, inlining, cache locality, and direct indexing before suggesting lower-level changes.

best_practices: Profile first, choose one hypothesis, change one thing, and compare with benchstat.
Prefer allocation reduction and algorithmic fixes before runtime tuning or unsafe code.
Document optimized hot paths with benchmark numbers and the reason for the pattern.
anti_patterns: Optimizing code from intuition without pprof, tracing, or benchmark evidence.
Applying many performance changes at once without isolating the effect of each change.
Using unsafe, pooling, or SIMD before proving a measured hot-path benefit.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it after profiling identifies a bottleneck or when reviewing Go code for likely performance risks.

faq.question: Does it write benchmarks for me?
faq.answer: It can guide benchmark design and comparison, but results must come from your project environment.

faq.question: Can it fix database latency?
faq.answer: It can identify external bottlenecks, but query tuning and schema design need database-specific guidance.

faq.question: Does it recommend unsafe optimizations?
faq.answer: Only after profiling and benchmarks show a meaningful hot-path gain that justifies the safety risk.

faq.question: Which Go areas does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers memory, CPU, runtime settings, networking, caching, batching, observability, and benchmark validation.

faq.question: Is it useful for Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. It is structured for Claude, Claude Code, and Codex workflows on Go repositories.
